brief: Build plant-products/CHED-PP as a SIBLING SET of live-animals inside trade-imports-animals-frontend — a new sets/plant-products/ tree served through a boot-time set switch (SERVED_SET=live-animals|plant-products, one set per Node process) rather than a standalone CDP application — plus a new /plant-products/ REST surface and Mongo schema in trade-imports-animals-backend. Everything is grounded in the trace-mined CHED-PP requirements at workareas/shared/trace-requirements/ched-pp/ (39 pages, 354 field rows, 310 validation messages; 8 conflict rulings closed by Sam on 2026-07-18) and in the Phase-C scaffold plan at frontend-plan/SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md. Pass 1 covers m0-m4: the backend schema and its tests, the platform seams that let a second set exist at all, the set scaffold and its records adapter, reference-data fixtures, and the MANUAL, OWN-ORG, HAPPY-PATH journey from the import-type entry filter through origin, purpose, the depth-3 commodity collection, additional details, transport, goods movement, contacts, accompanying-document metadata, traders and consignor, to review, declaration and confirmation, with a 12-spoke task-list hub and a notifications dashboard. m5 carries six buildable-in-the-tail stubs (CSV commodity branch, CUC billing, consignor address-book search, draft lifecycle delete/amend/copy, the Article 72 no-op rule hook, the auth stub) and five deferred stubs (the whole delegated-authority ownership/visibility/auto-population layer and its two pages, file bytes plus antivirus, and the cloning front door) — none of the eleven has been planned, and each must be planned before it is built. Integrations are stubbed throughout pass 1: fixed signed-in user and single stubbed organisation, allow-all permissions, fixture reference data, always-low risk, no certificate PDF, no Dynamics, no TRACES, no Notify. Post-submission is out of scope entirely.
source: workareas/shared/plant-products-ched-pp/recon/chedpp-requirements.md (8 rulings, 12-spoke hub, m5 + deferred ruling text)
workareas/shared/plant-products-ched-pp/frontend-plan/SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md (FD-1..FD-13, §1 file tree, §4 wiring, §5 P-1..P-8, §7 T-1..T-8, §8 gaps, §9 sequencing)
regenerationOf: workareas/shared/trace-requirements/ched-pp/backlog.json (re-expressed from a standalone CDP app onto the sibling-set architecture; inc-NNN -> pp-NNN)

scopeDecisions.decision: OUT of first pass. Pass 1 is a single-org, own-behalf journey. The ownership/visibility/auto-population tenancy layer (pp-048), consignment-for (pp-049) and consignment-organisation (pp-050) are deferred to a later programme; G-1..G-6 stay open for it.

IN first-pass scope (pp-043), gated provisionally on a free-standing isCuc flag per c-007. The trigger is NOT settled — possibly derived from the Sevington port server-side — so the gate condition must stay swappable, and confirming it with IPAFFS is an open external action.

OUT of first pass (pp-052). The success path was never observed — all three corpus traces hit the 406 'You cannot clone this certificate'; when re-opened, the success-state flow must be sourced first.

Build the REAL commodity search now (pp-023): commodity-code tree browse plus EPPO genus/species search as a pure server round-trip (POST -> 302 -> GET, zero client XHR), not a canned fixture code-pick. eppoCode is THE species join key (Open Q 1); add-species-<id> is transient UI state, never persisted. Fixture-backed lookup in pass 1, real integration later.

The hub has 12 spokes: Origin of the import, Purpose, Commodity, Additional details, Transport to the BCP, Goods movement services, Contact details, Nominated contacts (optional), Accompanying documents, Traders, Billing (conditional on isCuc), Review and submit. Catch certificates / charity / latest-health-cert sections are OMITTED (not evidenced for CHED-PP). The hub OWNS navigation ('Save and return to hub'); every mandatory section must be Completed before 'Review and submit' unlocks; optional spokes do not gate. SEQUENCING (added 2026-08-01): only ten of the twelve spokes have a planned m4 carrier. Spoke 11 (Billing) is produced by pp-043 — an m5 UNPLANNED stub that SD-12 forbids building without a planning pass — so the end of pass-1 m4 renders ELEVEN spokes (1-10 plus Review and submit). pp-029 builds the conditional-row code path (conditional: true + status NA omits the row) and pp-043 later appends the row, the flow section and sections/billing.js; no m0-m4 increment may reference a billing row, because taskRowById on a missing row throws.

Build a server-side placeholder rule hook (no-op) in pass 1 (pp-046) so Article 72 can be dropped in later without rework; the country x commodity condition and its journey effect are supplied by product later.

RULED MANDATORY — at least one document (a phytosanitary certificate) is required to submit; the accompanyingDocuments group carries minEntries 1 and blocks submit until satisfied (pp-034). The earlier isChedp/CHED-P trap reading is moot.

scopeDecisions.topic: Architecture — sibling set, not a standalone app
scopeDecisions.decision: NEW for this backlog, supersedes the source inc-001..inc-003 assumption. plant-products is a SIBLING SET under src/server/app/sets/plant-products/ in the existing trade-imports-animals-frontend, not a new CDP application. The source's 'scaffold a CDP app' (inc-001), 'Mongo persistence spine' (inc-002) and 'session/routing spine' (inc-003) are re-interpreted as pp-007 (set scaffold + L1 gateway), pp-008 (set-owned records adapter over the backend REST surface) and pp-009 (set flow/session spine).

scopeDecisions.topic: Architecture — boot-time set switch, not co-residency
scopeDecisions.decision: One set per Node process, selected at boot by SERVED_SET (values live-animals (default) | plant-products; FD-1). routes.js becomes the selector and is the ONLY reader of the env var; an unknown value is a loud boot failure. Co-residency (per-set URL BASE, keyed singletons, two sets in one process) is explicitly OUT of scope, which is why shared/paths.js is unchanged in pass 1 (FD-4).

scopeDecisions.topic: Persistence — set-owned records service against a backend REST surface
scopeDecisions.decision: Persistence is NOT a second L2 notification-mapper. The plant set owns sets/plant-products/services/records/ (stub.js + real.js + mapper/) injected through the existing configureRecords seam (FD-5), speaking to the Phase-B /plant-products/notifications REST surface in the Java backend. Whole-document PUT, last-write-wins, no ETag/If-Match (carried from the source deviation). configureCommodityReference is NOT called by the plant gateway. Nothing under sets/plant-products/ may import services/persistence/records/.

scopeDecisions.topic: Backend domain model — Lombok entities, records at the API boundary
scopeDecisions.decision: The backend plantproducts package follows the house model exactly: Lombok-annotated mutable domain/entity classes for the aggregate and its nested value classes (so MapStruct applyContent/toDto and the snapshot/copy mappers work), with Java records reserved for API-boundary DTO request/response shapes and small immutable results (e.g. ReplaceResult). Public records at service/audit boundaries get compact-constructor null guards. Repositories are scoped by package so the plantproducts Mongo repositories are picked up alongside animals (pp-002, the D-8 wiring gate).

scopeDecisions.topic: m5 is carried as stubs, not plans
scopeDecisions.decision: The eleven m5 entries (pp-042..pp-052) are carried as UNPLANNED stubs — six todo, five deferred. No planner ran over them, so their filesToTouch/obligations/acceptanceCriteria are deliberately empty and their notes carry only the ruling text. A build loop must NOT attempt any of them without a planning pass first; inventing detail for a stub is a defect.

Stubbed in pass 1 (integrations.md): Defra ID / customer (fixed signed-in user, single stubbed org), permissions (allow-all), field config (the CHED-PP set is inline), risk assessment (always low), certificate PDF, Dynamics 365, TRACES SOAP, GOV.UK Notify. OUT of scope entirely: post-submission (the BIP inspector decision-* app, post-submit Checks / Valid-Rejected tabs, inspection-required confirmation variants, split-consignment-confirm), file bytes + antivirus (metadata only), the economic-operator address book (consignor is free-typed).

scopeDecisions.topic: consignee = importer = the single stubbed org (pass 1)
scopeDecisions.decision: SCHEMA-DESIGN.md line 100 makes consignee an auto-populated owning-org operator (POP-3, server/stub-filled) and line 101 makes importer the same owning org (POP-1), but the Java backend fills only ownership.* (PlantProductsNotificationService STUB_ORGANISATION_ID 'stub-org' / STUB_ORGANISATION_NAME 'Stubbed organisation') — nothing writes consignee, so the document would ship with an empty consignee and 'Same as consignee' would resolve against nothing. RULED: in pass 1 consignee, importer and the 'Same as consignee' delivery-address source are ONE operator — the fixed stubbed organisation exported by sets/plant-products/services/stub-org.js (created by pp-007). pp-035's to-dto writes BOTH importer and consignee from stubOrganisationOperator() on every save; neither is ever an obligation and neither is folded back into answers. When the auth / delegated-authority layer lands (pp-047, pp-048) both moves server-side and the mapper writes are deleted.
scopeDecisions.carriedFrom: critic finding — consignee had no writer in either repo

deviations.deviation: The source's inc-001 (CDP app scaffold), inc-002 (Mongo persistence spine) and inc-003 (session/routing spine) are re-interpreted rather than carried: pp-007 builds the sibling-set skeleton plus the L1 gateway, pp-008 builds the set-owned records adapter over the backend REST surface, pp-009 completes the set's flow/session policy.
deviations.reason: The target architecture changed after the source backlog was written — plant-products is a sibling set inside an existing frontend, and persistence now lives in the Java backend, so a CDP scaffold and a frontend Mongo spine no longer exist as work.

deviations.deviation: Thirteen increments have no source increment at all (pp-001..pp-006, pp-010, pp-011, pp-012, pp-041, and the platform/test families folded into them).
deviations.reason: The sibling-set architecture creates work the standalone-app backlog never had: the Java backend schema and its stage-9 tests, the platform seams that let a second set exist (P-1 obligation-source policy injection, P-3 gateway split), the per-set test scaffolding (P-4/P-5/T-1..T-6) and the P-7 depth-3 characterisation gate.

deviations.deviation: pp-019 (origin-of-import) depends on pp-018 (country-of-origin), where the source had inc-009 and inc-010 in parallel.
deviations.reason: Both pages write sections/origin.js and share the origin flow section and task row that pp-018 creates; serialising them avoids a same-file conflict in the build loop.

deviations.deviation: Every m3 commodity increment (pp-022..pp-028) depends on pp-012, the P-7 depth-3 characterisation gate, in addition to its source dependencies.
deviations.reason: Depth 3 is unproven platform ground (the live exemplar animalIdentifiers is only depth 2). SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 rule 1 makes P-7 a hard precondition for all m3 work.

deviations.deviation: pp-018/pp-019/pp-020 (the first obligation-bearing pages) additionally depend on pp-010 (dep-cruiser rules + cloned app-root suites + contract table).
deviations.reason: SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 rule 2 — the policy seam and the cloned contract table must exist before the first obligation registers, or the first page increment cannot be verified two-sidedly.

deviations.deviation: Whole-document PUT on every save; no JSON-Patch, no ETag / If-Match optimistic concurrency. Two-tab editing is last-write-wins by deliberate decision (Open Q 3).
deviations.reason: Carried from the source deviations — IPAFFS's patch+etag protocol is not worth inheriting at pass-1 volumes, and the house backend already models whole-document replace.

deviations.deviation: One stable id; status moves DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> AMEND -> DELETED. The IPAFFS DRAFT.GB -> CHEDPP.GB id flip and dual-id URLs are rejected (c-028: own URL scheme, do not port /notification/vnet).
deviations.reason: Carried from the source deviations — the id flip is an IPAFFS implementation artefact, not a requirement, and it leaks into every URL and every reference caption.

deviations.deviation: govuk-frontend toolbox only — no bespoke CSS partials, no bespoke datepicker, CDP cookie banner rather than IPAFFS's implied-consent .global-cookie-message; real-href govuk-back-link, not a JS history back.
deviations.reason: Carried from the source deviations; also the workspace standing rule (stay inside the govuk-frontend toolbox).

deviations.deviation: Accessibility and error-copy defects are FIXED, not ported: GDS 'There is a problem' error-summary title everywhere (c-004), radios with the H1 inside the fieldset legend and the caption above (c-014), real <label> per control on commodity-bulk-details (never aria-label only), a real govuk-panel with an H1 on confirmation, and the c-010/c-011 consignor label fixes.
deviations.reason: Carried from the source deviations and rulings. These are once-recorded defaults, signed off in this backlog rather than re-litigated per increment.

deviations.deviation: Validation copy is single-layer: one canonical Joi-voice string per field ('Enter/Select the ...'), not the frontend+backend pair (c-018). Per-page acceptance criteria cite the backend 'Add the ...' variants only to reject them.
deviations.reason: Carried from the source ruling c-018; recorded once in pp-009 for the whole set.

deviations.deviation: The overdue-debtor gate is NOT ported to import-type (c-024).
deviations.reason: Ruled out of first pass — the IPAFFS GET/POST inconsistency is a latent bug, reported independently. pp-017 carries the do-NOT-port flag.

deviations.deviation: Enum values are normalised, not inherited from the IPAFFS wire format (e.g. reasonForImport is INTERNAL_MARKET | RE_ENTRY | RE_CONFORMITY_CHECK; c-006). Codes are stored, never display strings (country codes, package types, quantity types, document types, transport means, variety IDs).
deviations.reason: Carried from the source; the trace-mined wire values are IPAFFS-internal and would hard-code a legacy vocabulary into a new schema.

deviations.deviation: commodity.inputMethod is a persisted obligation, NOT a flow-only key; only importType and declaration are flow-only (FD-8).
deviations.reason: SCHEMA-DESIGN §1.1 gives inputMethod a home on the document, so it must ride the manifest like any other answer; the source backlog left this ambiguous.

deviations.deviation: Accompanying documents ride the answers tree as an accompanyingDocuments GROUP obligation in the frontend, while the backend keeps them in a separate accompanying-documents sub-resource; the set-owned records impl projects the group onto the sub-resource CRUD at save (naive list + delete + recreate is acceptable at pass-1 volumes) (FD-11).
deviations.reason: Keeps the frontend model uniform (one answers tree, engine-owned scope/wipe/completeness) while honouring the backend's separate-collection ruling. The projection is pp-034's to own; pp-008 lands the naive version.

deviations.deviation: The hub's spoke 12 (Review and submit) is a flow SECTION carrying the authored gate scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers, not a task row (FD-12); and flow sections OPEN with a start section containing the dashboard and import-type pages (FD-13).
deviations.reason: Exact live-animals precedent. The round-1 plan wrongly kept dashboard and import-type outside sections; the round-2 verifier corrected it against flow.js:32-36.

deviations.deviation: The stub records implementation must reproduce real semantics including status-transition legality, and PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE (stub|real, default real) is set-owned rather than reusing the L2 mode.js (FD-6).
deviations.reason: The Playwright ladder for the plant set runs self-hosted with no backend; L2's mode.js reading LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE is itself a (cosmetic) leak, noted as P-8 and not fixed in this pass.

deviations.deviation: Per-set app-root Vitest suites are CLONED as *.plant-products.test.js rather than parameterised, while the pure filesystem walkers (copy-convention, copy-parity) are parameterised in-file over both set roots (FD-10).
deviations.reason: Vitest isolates files into separate workers, so per-set FILES sidestep the single-slot configure* singletons; the fs walks touch no singleton and can loop in one file.

deviations.deviation: Two source m5 increments are re-scoped rather than carried verbatim: inc-042 (auth stub) formalises an org stub that m0-m4 already run with implicitly, and inc-038 (consignor-search) is a thin bypass stub rather than a built page.
deviations.reason: Pass 1 already assumes a fixed signed-in user and a single stubbed organisation from pp-007 onward, and the economic-operator address book is not built, so the search surface is always bypassed to 'Create new'.

deviations.deviation: pp-024 (commodity-basic-description) depends on pp-023 (commodity-search), where the source had them independent.
deviations.reason: pp-024, pp-025, pp-026 and pp-027 all EDIT features/commodities/{page.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js} — files pp-022 creates and pp-023 extends. pp-023 already carries pp-022 (and pp-021), so this single edge closes the whole chain and serialises the same-file work, exactly as DV-3 does for pp-018 -> pp-019.

sequencingNotes: HARD GATE 1 — pp-012 (P-7 depth-3 nested-collection characterisation test) must be GREEN before ANY m3 work starts. It composes a synthetic 3-deep manifest as an L2 fixture and exercises grouped-binding registration at depth 3, appendEntryAt/updateEntryAt/removeEntryAt, per-instance scope and wipe, collection-complete rollup and dispatch coverage inheritance. GREEN means the m3 commodity increments proceed on the platform as-is; ANY RED raises a NEW platform work item that must land before pp-021. Every m3 increment (pp-021..pp-028) carries pp-012 in dependsOn to make this unmissable.

HARD GATE 2 — pp-021 (commodity collection model extension) is a HALT-FOR-REVIEW model-extension gate, mirroring the source inc-012 nested-collection gate. The build loop must stop after pp-021, attach pp-012's characterisation evidence plus pp-021's own real-object characterisation suite, and wait for Sam's review of the depth-3 model before any commodity page (pp-022 onward collects it) proceeds.

Platform increments land before the set scaffold: pp-005 (P-1 obligation-source policy injection) and pp-006 (P-3 L1 gateway split) have no dependencies and are pure behaviour-preserving refactors of live-animals wiring, verifiable against the existing suite before any plant code exists. pp-007 (set scaffold) depends on both.

Platform items land before the first obligation-bearing page (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 rule 2): pp-010 (dep-cruiser rules, cloned app-root suites, contract table) is a dependency of pp-018/pp-019/pp-020 because the policy seam and cloned contract table must exist for the first obligation to register cleanly.

TWO-SIDED VERIFICATION on every platform-touching increment: it is not enough that the plant set is green. Every increment that edits anything outside sets/plant-products/ (pp-005, pp-006, pp-010, pp-011, and any platform work pp-012 raises) must also prove live-animals is unchanged — the full existing live-animals suite green, SERVED_SET unset still serving live-animals exactly as today, no existing-suite test-count drop, and the dep-cruiser violations baseline NOT regenerated.

The gaps G-A..G-I mean several increments TRANSPOSE from live exemplars rather than follow a recipe. pp-007 (there is no add-a-set recipe — this plan IS it), pp-008 (no records-adapter recipe), pp-009 (no entry-guard/opening-run authoring recipe), pp-017 and pp-039 (no flow-only-key recipe — transpose import-type-filter and declaration), pp-021/pp-025 (no depth-3 collection recipe), pp-029 (no create-the-hub-from-scratch recipe), pp-037 and pp-045 (no dashboard/lifecycle recipe), pp-038 (no check-answers-from-scratch recipe) and pp-042 (no CSV-branch recipe anywhere) must treat the gap text as first-class plan content and cite concrete live-animals files, not recipe steps.

Increment order in this array is topological and every dependsOn edge points EARLIER IN THE ARRAY (pp-010 and pp-011 are ordered immediately after pp-007, ahead of pp-008/pp-009, because nearly every later increment runs the test:plant-products / test:features:plant-products scripts they create — so their ids are deliberately out of numeric order), so the graph is acyclic by construction and the array can be walked front to back.

m1 reference data (pp-013..pp-016) all depend only on pp-007 and can run in any order or in parallel once the scaffold boots. The commodity-code + EPPO-species fixture (pp-014) is the ONE lookup that eventually goes real — ship a ~10-code fixture with species now.

The §2.3 flow sections array fixes the append order (start, origin, purpose, commodities, additional-details, transport, goods-movement, contacts, nominated-contacts, documents, parties, [billing], review); §2.1 fixes the canonical row ids and hub GROUPS. Rows for not-yet-built sections land WITH their section increment, not with pp-029.

c-004 (error-summary title) and c-014 (radio a11y) are NOT per-page blockers: every page ships the adopted GDS default and the sign-off is recorded once in this backlog, never re-litigated per increment.

Every page increment follows the add-a-page / add-a-section / add-a-collection recipes with the SIBLING-SET-PLAN §7 plant verification ladder substituted, and adds its valid-POST case to contract.plant-products.test.js (T-5 standing rule).
m5 (pp-042..pp-052) is UNPLANNED. Do not build any of it from this backlog — each stub needs a planning pass first. Five of the eleven are deferred out of first-pass scope altogether.

obligations[].id in this backlog IS the code-level obligation NAME as it will exist under sets/plant-products/obligations/** — path-safe camelCase (commodityLines, varietyClass, destinationAddressLine1, intendedForFinalUsers). It is never a slug and never kebab-case. Kebab strings elsewhere in an increment (collectedBy, page/route references, e2e slugs) are PAGE SLUGS — a different namespace that stays kebab.

The test scaffolding is a hard dependency, not a convenience: pp-010 creates the test:plant-products script and contract.plant-products.test.js, pp-011 creates test:features:plant-products and the per-set Playwright project. Neither script exists in the frontend package.json today, so EVERY increment whose verification ladder runs them (or whose filesToTouch includes contract.plant-products.test.js) carries pp-010 and/or pp-011 in dependsOn — no increment may hedge with 'if the script has landed'.

gaps.gap: No 'add a set' recipe exists — SIBLING-SET-PLAN IS the recipe for plant-products (set name + SERVED_SET contract, L3/L4 skeletons, the 13-row gateway call table, selector registration, dep-cruiser edits, per-set test scripts, set services, minimal usable surfaces, two-sided ladder). Bites pp-007.

No depth-3 nested-collection recipe — add-a-collection's nested exemplar (animalIdentifiers) is only depth 2. Needs grouped-binding groups arrays of length 3, ...At path discipline, parent-index validation at TWO levels, and scope/wipe/completeness at depth. Unproven platform ground until pp-012 is green. Bites pp-012, pp-021, pp-025.

No 'create the hub from scratch' recipe — recipe §3.6 assumes an existing hub. Needs the controller GROUPS shape, numbered group captions in both locales, row title/hint copy contract, conditional:true hide semantics, review-spoke unlock wiring and hub axe/e2e baselines; transpose the live-animals hub feature file-for-file. Bites pp-007 (skeleton) and pp-029 (full build).

No records-adapter recipe — the recipes' persistence step ('edit the L2 notification-mapper') is inapplicable under FD-5. Needs the 11-op engine port surface, the op->HTTP table, stub/real parity including status-transition legality, mapper omission-assertion discipline (a field with no backend home gets an explicit omission test, never an invented property) and the documents sub-resource projection. Bites pp-008.

No entry-guard / opening-run authoring recipe — flow maintenance covers CHANGING flow data, not authoring entry-guard.js and run.js from nothing. Needs the policy contract: what entryGuardTarget may return, its allowed L2 reads, deep-link redirect policy, and which pages belong in RUN_STEPS. Bites pp-009.

No check-answers-from-scratch recipe — the recipes extend existing cards. Creating features/check-answers/ needs the view-model/cards directory contract, row()/changeAction() obligation-name resolution through dispatch, scope-driven row omission and the review -> declaration -> confirmation exit spine; transpose the live-animals feature. Bites pp-038.

No dashboard/lifecycle recipe — notifications-dashboard, delete-notification and the amend/copy actions have live exemplars (features/dashboard, features/notification-actions, features/delete-notification) but no recipe doc; plan by exemplar transposition citing concrete live-animals files. Bites pp-037 and pp-045.

No flow-only-key recipe — import-type and declaration ride FLOW_ONLY_KEYS/session, not the manifest (FD-8). Recipe fragments exist but no end-to-end script (key -> session store -> entry filter behaviour -> finalise-time inclusion); transpose the import-type-filter and declaration features. Bites pp-009, pp-017, pp-039.

No CSV-branch recipe anywhere — the branch-replacement pattern (same 12 obligations, alternate collection surface) has no live-animals analogue at all. An m5 problem, flagged now so nobody expects a recipe. Bites pp-042.

milestones.name: Backend schema, platform seams & set scaffold
milestones.goal: The Java /plant-products/ schema and REST surface plus its stage-9 unit and integration tests; the two platform seams that let a second set exist (obligation-source policy injected via the set manifest, the L1 gateway split into per-set route files behind a SERVED_SET selector); the sets/plant-products/ skeleton booting under SERVED_SET=plant-products with a stub records service; the set-owned records adapter against the backend REST surface; the set's flow/session spine (entry guard, opening run, draft save/resume); the per-set test scaffolding (dep-cruiser rules, cloned app-root suites, Vitest and Playwright scripts, empty contract table); and the P-7 depth-3 characterisation gate.

milestones.name: Reference data
milestones.goal: Set-owned fixture modules under sets/plant-products/services/ — countries (~254 with UK subdivisions and the c-012 Republic of Ireland label, modelled with real optgroups); commodity codes + EPPO species + variety/class applicability (the ONE lookup that eventually goes real); BCPs + per-BCP inspection premises; and the measure/document catalogues (package types, quantity types, document types with the c-016 Sea waybill dedupe, transport options, gross-volume units, reasons for import). All store codes, never display strings.

milestones.name: Consignment basics
milestones.goal: The certificate-type entry filter built out to its full spec (flow-only, do NOT port the overdue-debtor gate), then the first obligation-bearing pages and the first hub spokes: country of origin, origin of import (countries + internal reference), and the main reason for import as a normalised enum.

milestones.name: Commodity capture (manual)
milestones.goal: The hard part — the depth-3 nested repeating commodity model (commodityLines -> species -> varieties) landed as a HALT-FOR-REVIEW model extension behind the P-7 gate, then the manual branch: input-method routing, real commodity-code tree browse + EPPO species search, species selection, variety and class at depth 3, the commodity summary table with remove, per-commodity measures, and the consignment additional-details totals with derived rollups.

milestones.name: Details, contacts, traders, review & submit
milestones.goal: The task-list hub built out to the ELEVEN spokes that exist by the end of m4 — spokes 1-10 plus Review and submit; the conditional Billing spoke (11) is carried by pp-043, an m5 unplanned stub, so pass-1 m4 deliberately closes on an 11-spoke hub; transport to the BCP with the containers collection; goods-movement services; responsible-person and nominated contacts; accompanying-document metadata projected onto the backend sub-resource; traders and the hand-entered consignor; the notifications dashboard; then check-your-answers, declaration and confirmation — closing the manual, own-org happy path, proven end to end by a whole-journey E2E fixture and a per-set Playwright split.

milestones.name: Variants & deferred (UNPLANNED STUBS)
milestones.goal: Carried as stubs only — none has been planned and none may be built without a planning pass. todo: the CSV commodity branch, the CUC billing sub-journey, the consignor address-book search bypass, draft lifecycle (soft-delete / amend / copy-as-new), the Article 72 no-op rule hook, and the formalised auth stub. deferred out of first-pass scope: the delegated-authority ownership/visibility/auto-population layer and its two pages, document file bytes + antivirus, and the cloning front door.

increments.title: Backend: plant-products schema skeleton (aggregate, REST surface, minting, wiring stages 1-8)
increments.recipe: workareas/shared/plant-products-ched-pp/backend-schema/SCHEMA-DESIGN.md §1-§6, stages 1-8

filesToTouch.what: Static test-data factory (private ctor, static methods only) mirroring the role of animals' utils/NotificationTestData. Exports: fullyPopulatedDto() and fullyPopulatedNotification() building every content area of the aggregate with realistic CHED-PP values — origin (countryCode 'BR', countryOfConsignmentCode 'BR', internalReference), reasonForImport INTERNAL_MARKET, commodity with inputMethod MANUAL and a depth-3 commodityComplement (1 CommodityLine with 2 PlantSpecies, one species carrying 1 SpeciesVariety with varietyClass CLASS_I) including BigDecimal quantity/netWeight, additionalDetails (totalGrossWeight, grossVolume, grossVolumeUnit LITRES), consignor/consignee/importer/destination/packer PlantProductsOperator with full PlantProductsAddress, responsiblePerson + 1 nominatedContact (PlantProductsContact), transport (borderControlPost, inspectionPremises, meansOfTransport VESSEL, arrivalDate LocalDate, arrivalTime '14:30', usesContainers true + 1 TransportContainer), goodsMovementServices (ADD_MRN_NOW + 18-char MRN + usingGvms), isCuc false, billing, declaration. Also refNumber(String suffix) helper returning 'GBN-PP-26-' + suffix values matching REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN. Used by mapper/snapshot/copy-mapper/service/controller tests so full-aggregate fixtures are declared once. Zero imports from the animals package.

Mirror animals ReferenceNumberGeneratorTest. Assert: generate() output matches PlantProductsReferenceNumberGenerator.REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN ('^GBN-PP-\\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$'); YY segment equals the current two-digit year; body chars drawn only from the Crockford base32 alphabet (no I, L, O, U); a batch of generations (e.g. 100) all match the pattern and are not all identical (randomness smoke — no distribution assertions).

Mirror animals NotificationSortTest (plain JUnit, no Spring). toSort mapping table: 'arrivalDate' -> property 'transport.arrivalDate'; 'createdAt' -> 'created'; explicit ',asc'/',desc' direction parsing; default sort (transport.arrivalDate desc) for null, empty, unknown field name and malformed direction inputs. One test per behaviour, not per input permutation — parameterise the fallback cases.

ONE consolidated class (decision recorded in notes) satisfying the per-enum rule: for EACH of the 8 enums (PlantProductsNotificationStatus, ReasonForImport, CommodityInputMethod, FinishedOrPropagated, VarietyClass, GrossVolumeUnit, PlantProductsMeansOfTransport, CommonTransitConvention) exactly one Jackson round-trip test (serialise one representative constant -> JSON string -> deserialise -> same constant, via a shared ObjectMapper) and one unknown-value negative test (readValue of a JSON string with a non-constant value throws InvalidFormatException/ValueInstantiationException). Use @ParameterizedTest over the enum classes where the shape is identical. NEVER one test per enum constant (feedback_no_per_enum_round_trip_tests).

Mirror animals NotificationMapperTest; obtain the MapStruct impl via Mappers.getMapper(PlantProductsNotificationMapper.class) (or new PlantProductsNotificationMapperImpl() if the house test does that — match the exemplar). Assert: applyContent(dto, entity) copies every content field group from PlantProductsNotificationTestData.fullyPopulatedDto() onto a fresh entity (spot-assert one leaf per group INCLUDING the depth-3 varieties leaf and BigDecimal fields); applyContent NEVER overwrites server-set fields — pre-stamp entity id/referenceNumber/chedType/status/ownership/created/updated/submittedBaseline/expireAt, put conflicting values in the dto where the dto surface allows, assert the entity keeps the pre-stamped values; toDto(entity) maps all content fields plus the visible server-set fields (referenceNumber, chedType, status, created, updated) and NEVER exposes submittedBaseline/expireAt (not on the DTO type — assert via mapped-field values only); null nested objects/lists survive both directions without NPE.

Mirror animals NotificationContentSnapshotTest (house-parity addition to the 9-item stage-9 list — see notes). Assert: from(notification) captures all 16 amendable content fields (origin, reasonForImport, commodity, additionalDetails, consignor, consignee, importer, destination, packer, responsiblePerson, nominatedContacts, transport, goodsMovementServices, isCuc, billing, declaration); the snapshot is a DEEP clone — mutating the source notification's nested commodity line / nominatedContacts after from() leaves the snapshot unchanged; applyTo(target) restores all 16 fields onto a differently-populated notification while leaving id, referenceNumber, chedType, status, ownership, created, updated, submittedBaseline, expireAt untouched; null lists on the source normalise to empty lists in the snapshot (house parity).

Mirror animals NotificationCopyMapperTest. Drive copyFrom(source) with fullyPopulatedNotification() in SUBMITTED state carrying a submittedBaseline, expireAt, declaration. Assert the D-19 table field-by-field — RESET: id null, referenceNumber null (service re-mints), status DRAFT, declaration null, submittedBaseline null, expireAt reset, created/updated set to ~now (assert within a tolerance window or non-null-and-after-test-start, matching the exemplar's idiom); RETAIN: all content field groups equal source (spot-assert one leaf per group incl. the depth-3 varieties leaf) plus ownership retained; DEEP copy — mutating the source's nested species list after copyFrom leaves the copy unchanged.

The highest-value class; mirror animals NotificationServiceTest structure (@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), @Mock PlantProductsNotificationRepository/PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository/PlantProductsNotificationMapper/PlantProductsNotificationCopyMapper/PlantProductsReferenceNumberGenerator/PlantProductsNotificationTtlConfig, service built by constructor with listPageSize e.g. 25; @Nested per operation). CREATE: dto with a referenceNumber -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; happy path mints via generator, status DRAFT, chedType 'CHEDPP', ownership stubbed (assignedOrganisationId 'stub-org', name 'Stubbed organisation'), created/updated stamped, expiry stamped from ttlConfig, mapper.applyContent invoked, saved entity returned; DuplicateKeyException on save retries with a fresh mint up to MAX_REF_RETRIES=3 then IllegalStateException (verify generator called 3 times). REPLACE: path/body referenceNumber mismatch -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; unknown ref -> upsert path creates (ReplaceResult.created true, server fields stamped); existing SUBMITTED or DELETED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (writable = DRAFT/AMEND only); existing DRAFT -> content applied, updated re-stamped, created false. FIND: delegates to findByReferenceNumber. FINDALL: 1-based page converts to 0-based PageRequest with listPageSize and PlantProductsNotificationSort.toSort; status filter is exactly DRAFT/SUBMITTED/AMEND (DELETED hidden); referenceNumber param trims and exact-matches to a single-row page via findByReferenceNumberAndStatusIn, empty page when absent; response page number is 1-based. CHANGESTATUS — the five-row transition table, one test per row plus negatives: DRAFT->SUBMITTED captures submittedBaseline from current content; SUBMITTED->AMEND captures submittedBaseline; AMEND->SUBMITTED with discardChanges null/false re-captures the baseline from amended content; AMEND->SUBMITTED with discardChanges true restores content via snapshot applyTo and keeps the old baseline; DRAFT/SUBMITTED/AMEND->DELETED soft-deletes; DELETED->DELETED is idempotent (200-equivalent, no exception); every transition not in the table -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (parameterise the illegal from/to pairs); discardChanges=true on any transition other than AMEND->SUBMITTED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; unknown ref -> PlantProductsNotFoundException. COPY: delegates to copyMapper.copyFrom, re-mints a fresh reference (with the same 3-retry DuplicateKeyException loop), returns a new DRAFT; source in DRAFT or DELETED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (copyable = SUBMITTED/AMEND); unknown ref -> PlantProductsNotFoundException; verify NO writes to the accompanying-document repository (copies start documentless, D-19). Verify @Transactional semantics only by behaviour, not annotation reflection.

Mirror animals NotificationControllerTest: @WebMvcTest(PlantProductsNotificationController.class) + @TestPropertySource(properties = {"admin.secret=test-secret", "app.base-url=http://localhost:8085"}) (same two properties the house slice needs — the animals servlet filter rides every slice); @MockitoBean PlantProductsNotificationService, PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentService and PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentMapper (the controller's constructor deps). Reference constants like 'GBN-PP-26-ABC001'. Tests: POST /plant-products/notifications -> 201 with Location ending /plant-products/notifications/{ref} and body JSON; service BadRequest -> 400; PUT /{ref} -> 200 on replace, 201 + Location when ReplaceResult.created, 400 on mismatch (service throws); GET /{ref} -> 200 PlantProductsNotificationResponse embedding accompanyingDocuments array, 404 when service returns empty (PlantProductsNotFoundException -> handler); GET list -> 200 with page/sort/referenceNumber params passed through to service and JSON page envelope fields (content, page, pageSize, totalElements, totalPages); PUT /{ref}/status with {"status":"SUBMITTED"} -> 200, missing status -> 400 (bean validation on StatusChangeRequest), illegal transition (service throws BadRequest) -> 400, unknown ref -> 404; POST /{ref}/copies -> 201 + Location, 400 not copyable, 404; malformed reference number path variable (fails @Pattern) -> 400 on ANY endpoint (one representative test); error bodies are the handler's problem-style shape with no stack trace content. This class is also the de-facto unit coverage of PlantProductsExceptionHandler (decision in notes — no separate handler test).

MockitoExtension unit test of PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentService (mock PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository + PlantProductsNotificationRepository/PlantProductsNotificationService as the production constructor requires — read the production class first). Tests: list returns the repository's documents for the notification, throws PlantProductsNotFoundException when the notification reference is unknown; create derives notificationReferenceNumber from the path argument NEVER the body (a body-supplied value is ignored/overwritten), stamps created/updated, only allowed while the notification is writable (DRAFT/AMEND) — SUBMITTED/DELETED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; replace looks the document up via findByIdAndNotificationReferenceNumber and 404s when the doc is not under this notification, re-stamps updated, same writability guard; delete removes via the scoped lookup, PlantProductsNotFoundException when absent, same writability guard.

@WebMvcTest(PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentController.class) + the same @TestPropertySource pair; @MockitoBean the document service (+ mapper if constructor-injected). Base path /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/accompanying-documents. Tests: GET -> 200 with the wrapped {"documents":[...]} envelope (never a bare array — assert jsonPath $.documents), 404 when notification unknown; POST valid dto -> 201 + Location of the created document, 400 when notification not writable (service throws BadRequest), 404 notification unknown; PUT /{document-id} -> 200, 404 when the doc is not under this notification; DELETE /{document-id} -> 204 empty body, 404 when absent; malformed notification reference (fails @Pattern) -> 400.

Mirror animals NotificationExpirySweeperTest (MockitoExtension; mock PlantProductsNotificationRepository, PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository, the LockingTaskExecutor collaborator — stub the executor to run the task inline, exactly as the house test does). Tests: sweep queries findExpired with ~now and the configured batch Pageable; for each expired reference deletes the notification AND cascades accompanyingDocumentRepository.deleteByNotificationReferenceNumber (verify per-ref); no expired rows -> zero delete calls; batch bound respected (Pageable size from config); work runs under the shedlock lock (executor invoked).

Mirror animals NotificationExpirySweeperConditionTest using ApplicationContextRunner over PlantProductsAutoConfiguration (or the sweeper's own @Configuration surface, matching the exemplar): bean ABSENT when plant-products.notification.ttl.sweep.enabled is unset (no matchIfMissing) and when explicitly false; bean PRESENT when true. Stub the collaborator beans the context needs.

filesToTouch.what: Full-stack lifecycle IT, `class PlantProductsNotificationIT extends IntegrationBase` (same package as the animals ITs — the recorded D-6 test exception). Constants: ENDPOINT = "/plant-products/notifications"; REF regex from PlantProductsReferenceNumberGenerator.REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN (^GBN-PP-\\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$); a NONEXISTENT_REF like "GBN-PP-00-000000". @Autowired PlantProductsNotificationRepository + PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository; @BeforeEach deleteAll() on both (mirror NotificationIT.setUp). All HTTP via webClient("NoAuth") from IntegrationBase. Private fixture builder producing a FULL PlantProductsNotificationDto exercising the depth-3 nesting: origin{countryCode,countryOfConsignmentCode,internalReference}, reasonForImport, commodity{name,inputMethod,commodityComplement:[CommodityLine{commodityCode,commodityDescription,numberOfPackages,packageType,quantity,quantityType,netWeight,controlledAtmosphereContainer,finishedOrPropagated,intendedForFinalUsers,testAndTrial,species:[PlantSpecies{eppoCode,genusAndSpecies,speciesId,varieties:[SpeciesVariety{variety,varietyClass}]}]}]}, additionalDetails{totalGrossWeight,grossVolume,grossVolumeUnit}, consignor/consignee/importer/destination/packer (PlantProductsOperator with PlantProductsAddress incl. addressLine3), responsiblePerson, nominatedContacts, transport{borderControlPost,inspectionPremises,meansOfTransport,transportIdentification,transportDocumentReference,arrivalDate,arrivalTime "HH:mm" String,usesContainers,containers:[TransportContainer]}, goodsMovementServices{commonTransitConvention,movementReferenceNumber,usingGvms}, isCuc, billing, declaration. Tests: (1) POST blank-ref → 201 + Location header, minted ref matches regex, status=DRAFT, chedType="CHEDPP", ownership={assignedOrganisationId:"stub-org",assignedOrganisationName:"Stubbed organisation"}, created/updated non-null, every content field round-trips incl. varieties depth 3 (assert via GET reload, not just the POST body); (2) POST with body-supplied referenceNumber → 400; (3) PUT {ref} with matching body ref → 200 replaced content; (4) PUT with path/body ref mismatch → 400; (5) PUT to an unknown well-formed ref → 201 created (+Location, upsert per §3.1); (6) GET {ref} → 200 PlantProductsNotificationResponse embedding accompanyingDocuments (empty list when none); GET NONEXISTENT_REF → 404; malformed ref → 400 (@Pattern guard); (7) list GET ?page&sort&referenceNumber: 1-based page metadata, exact-match referenceNumber filter returns single row, DELETED rows hidden; (8) lifecycle happy chain in one test (mirror NotificationIT style): PUT status {SUBMITTED} → 200, then repository read proves submittedBaseline captured (it is @JsonIgnore — assert via PlantProductsNotificationRepository.findByReferenceNumber); PUT status {AMEND} → 200; content PUT edits a field while AMEND → 200; PUT status {SUBMITTED, discardChanges:true} → 200 and GET proves pre-amend content restored (cancel-amend, D-4); re-amend + edit + PUT status {SUBMITTED} (no flag) → 200 and GET proves amended content kept (baseline re-captured); (9) content PUT against SUBMITTED → 400 (not writable); (10) illegal transitions → 400 (at least DRAFT→AMEND and SUBMITTED→SUBMITTED); discardChanges:true on DRAFT→SUBMITTED → 400; (11) POST {ref}/copies on a SUBMITTED source → 201, new DRAFT with NEW minted ref, content fields retained, declaration null, accompanying documents NOT copied (D-19), source untouched; copies of a DRAFT source → 400; copies of NONEXISTENT_REF → 404; (12) PUT status {DELETED} from DRAFT/SUBMITTED → 200, repeat on already-DELETED → 200 (idempotent), deleted ref absent from list; (13) status change on NONEXISTENT_REF → 404; StatusChangeRequest with null status → 400 (bean validation).

Document sub-resource CRUD IT, extends IntegrationBase, same package. @Autowired PlantProductsNotificationRepository + PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository, @BeforeEach deleteAll() both. Helper: create a parent notification via POST /plant-products/notifications (blank ref) and capture the minted ref; base path …/{ref}/accompanying-documents. Tests: (1) GET list on fresh notification → 200 body { documents: [] } (never a bare array); (2) GET/POST against an unknown notification ref → 404; (3) POST PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentDto {documentType,documentReference,issueDate,files:[DocumentFile{fileId,filename}]} → 201 + Location, response echoes fields, repository row carries notificationReferenceNumber derived FROM THE PATH (assert a divergent body-supplied notification ref, if the DTO had one, is ignored — the DTO has no such field, so assert the persisted FK equals the path ref); (4) GET list → the created doc; (5) PUT …/{document-id} with changed fields → 200 updated (repository confirms); (6) PUT/DELETE with a document id belonging to a DIFFERENT notification → 404 (findByIdAndNotificationReferenceNumber guard); (7) DELETE …/{document-id} → 204 and list is empty; DELETE unknown id → 404; (8) writability guard: transition the notification to SUBMITTED via PUT …/status, then POST/PUT/DELETE a document → 400; transition to AMEND → document writes succeed again (writable in DRAFT and AMEND only).

Expiry-sweep IT mirroring NotificationExpiryIT verbatim in shape: extends IntegrationBase; @Autowired PlantProductsNotificationService + PlantProductsNotificationRepository + PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository; @BeforeEach deleteAll() both; calls plantProductsNotificationService.deleteExpired(batchSize) DIRECTLY (deterministic — never waits on the scheduled PlantProductsNotificationExpirySweeper). Private savers building PlantProductsNotification.builder().referenceNumber(ref).status(DRAFT).expireAt(x).build() and PlantProductsAccompanyingDocument.builder().notificationReferenceNumber(ref)… refs like "GBN-PP-26-EXP001". Tests: (1) deleteExpired removes the due notification AND cascades to plant_products_accompanying_documents by notificationReferenceNumber, while a non-due notification and its document survive; (2) null expireAt is never swept (deleteExpired returns 0, row survives); (3) batch bound: 3 due rows, deleteExpired(2) → 2 then deleteExpired(2) → 1, collection empties; (4) isolation: an animals-collection Notification row (animals NotificationRepository) with a due expireAt is NOT touched by the plant sweep — proves the cascade is scoped to the plant collections (and, via the @Autowired mix of animals + plantproducts repositories in one Spring context, proves the D-8 dual-package repository scan end to end).

increments.notes: Rationale: these 3 ITs are the executable contract the frontend records adapter (pp-008) codes against — the op→HTTP table in SIBLING-SET-PLAN §6.2 maps engine port ops onto exactly the endpoints/status codes these tests pin (create→POST 201, replaceFulfilment→PUT, finalise/amend/cancelAmend/softDelete→PUT …/status, copy→POST …/copies). Production code already exists (pp-001 commit a7961ac, pp-002 commit 75763b9); verified live: PlantProductsNotificationService exposes create/replace/find/findAll/changeStatus/copy/deleteExpired(int)/isWritable, CHED_TYPE="CHEDPP", STUB_ORGANISATION_ID="stub-org", STUB_ORGANISATION_NAME="Stubbed organisation". Exemplars (match their idiom, do not invent): integration/NotificationIT.java (webClient("NoAuth") WebTestClient flow, @BeforeEach repository cleanup, REF_FORMAT_REGEX constant from the generator, full-DTO builder + reload-assert pattern), integration/NotificationExpiryIT.java (direct service.deleteExpired call for determinism — its Javadoc explains why, mirror it), integration/document/DocumentControllerIT.java (sub-resource pattern), IntegrationBase.java (shared static Testcontainers: mongo:7.0 replica set + MockServer + OAuth mock; no per-IT container config needed). Decisions applied: D-3/D-4 (noun status endpoint + discardChanges disambiguation — the tests assert the NEW noun surface, never the animals action paths), D-6 (ITs are the one sanctioned animals-package touchpoint), D-8 (test 4 of the expiry IT + full-verify animals-IT green is the wiring gate), D-13 (no obligation enforcement asserted — submit succeeds without declaration.agreed; do NOT test frontend rules), D-19 (copy resets documents/declaration, retains content). Fixture values: use plausible CHED-PP codes consistent with obligation-field-map.md (e.g. eppoCode-style strings, package-type codes) but any string round-trips — the backend is draft-nullable and unvalidated by design. Decision (headless): no shared PlantProductsNotificationTestData class — pp-003 (units) and pp-004 are independent siblings both depending only on pp-002, so a shared helper would create a same-file conflict; each IT builds its own private fixtures (NotificationExpiryIT precedent). Decision: focused Failsafe run first (-Dit.test='PlantProducts*IT') for the inner loop, then the full mvn verify as the two-sided check (plant ITs + animals ITs green). mvn verify needs Docker running (Testcontainers). Run output to a scratch file and read once (run-tests-to-file rule).

(2) SPECIES_BY_CODE — { [leafCode]: [{ eppoCode, genusAndSpecies, speciesId }] }, >=1 species per plant leaf code, values mined from workareas/shared/trace-requirements/ched-pp/pages/commodity-basic-description.json (observed EPPO codes: CIDAC='Citrus australasica' under 08059000; PHAAN, LENCU, CXQDA, GYPEL as evidenced there; machinery codes 84321000 and 87019510 carry the placeholder EPPO 'NNNXX' per the species-checkbox variant evidence); speciesId is a stable fixture string (round-trip only — transient per Open Q 1, eppoCode is THE join key). (3) VARIETIES_BY_EPPO — { [eppoCode]: [{ id, label }] }; CIDAC gets the trace-observed list (single option label 'None', id 'NONE' — variety-of-genus-and-species.json evidence; 'Other' is a page affordance, NOT a fixture variety); exactly ONE additional species gets a multi-entry real-world variety list (e.g. Malus domestica cultivars if the ch-08 apples code carries a MABSD-family species) so pp-025 can exercise a real select — flagged as fixture-invented in a code-free way (see openQuestions, no in-file migration comments). (4) CLASSES_BY_EPPO — { [eppoCode]: subset of ['CLASS_I','CLASS_II','EXTRA_CLASS'] }; CIDAC gets all three (trace-observed options 'Class I'/'Class II'/'Extra Class'); species without class data are simply absent (=> N/A, varietyClass null per §3.1). (5) CLASS_LABELS — { CLASS_I: 'Class I', CLASS_II: 'Class II', EXTRA_CLASS: 'Extra Class' }. All consts Object.freeze'd.

The lookup barrel (§6.1: 'pure lookup barrel (index.js) over fixture.js'), mirroring the arrow-function-per-lookup style of sets/live-animals/services/commodities/index.js. Exports (all pure, synchronous, importing ONLY ./fixture.js): commodityTree() => COMMODITY_TREE; childrenOf(parentCode) => that node's children array, or the chapter list when parentCode is nullish (backs the pp-023 drill-down: root shows chapters, name=parent_<code> descends); commodityCodes() => flat array of leaf codes; isCommodityCode(code); descriptionFor(code) => leaf description (consumed by the records mapper for ref-data-derived commodityDescription, and by commodity-summary); speciesFor(code) => SPECIES_BY_CODE[code] ?? []; genusAndSpeciesFor(eppoCode) => label lookup across all species entries; isSpeciesOf(code, eppoCode); searchSpecies({ genus, eppoCode }) => case-insensitive combined filter (genus substring on genusAndSpecies AND eppoCode prefix/exact when given — the trace submits genus and eppo-code together as ONE combined filter) returning [{ commodityCode, eppoCode, genusAndSpecies, speciesId }]; varietiesFor(eppoCode) => VARIETIES_BY_EPPO[eppoCode] ?? []; varietyLabelFor(eppoCode, varietyId); classesFor(eppoCode) => CLASSES_BY_EPPO[eppoCode] ?? []; classLabelFor(classCode) => CLASS_LABELS[classCode]; hasVarietyAndClass(eppoCode) => varietiesFor(eppoCode).length > 0 && classesFor(eppoCode).length > 0 (the pp-025 render gate: the legacy template renders a species' variety/class table ONLY when both option lists are non-empty). Unknown inputs return []/undefined — never throw.

Vitest unit suite pinning the fixture contract (test on input/output, no mocking — pure module): (1) commodityTree() has exactly 11 chapter nodes with codes ['06','07','08','09','10','12','14','25','38','84','87']; (2) commodityCodes() returns the mined leaf set, every leaf isCommodityCode(code)===true, and descriptionFor round-trips a known code; (3) childrenOf() with no argument returns the 11 chapters, childrenOf('06') returns chapter 06's children; (4) speciesFor('08059000') contains { eppoCode: 'CIDAC', genusAndSpecies: 'Citrus australasica' }; speciesFor for a machinery code (84321000) yields the NNNXX placeholder entry; (5) searchSpecies({ genus: 'citrus' }) finds CIDAC with its owning commodityCode, searchSpecies({ eppoCode: 'CIDAC' }) ditto, and the combined filter narrows; (6) varietiesFor('CIDAC') includes the 'None' option and classesFor('CIDAC') equals ['CLASS_I','CLASS_II','EXTRA_CLASS']; classLabelFor('EXTRA_CLASS') === 'Extra Class'; (7) the one multi-variety species: varietiesFor returns >1 entries each with stable id !== label, and varietyLabelFor resolves an id; (8) hasVarietyAndClass true for CIDAC, false for a species with no variety data AND false for an unknown eppoCode; (9) negative paths: speciesFor/varietiesFor/classesFor on unknown keys return [], descriptionFor/genusAndSpeciesFor return undefined, nothing throws. NO per-entry enumeration tests (one representative + one negative per lookup — do not scale tests with fixture size).

GET: state.get() ONCE; build the view via view-model/summary-groups.js (below); render with kit.base(), pass journey so the reference strip renders; back link hubPath(journey.journeyId). POST branches on the submit control (documents/consignment-details idiom — the Remove is a branch of the SAME POST so the crumb travels and no GET can delete): (a) payload.action matching 'remove:<lineIndex>:<speciesIndex>' -> delegate to remove/post-remove.js, then redirect back to this page via kit.withChangeContext(request, <own path>); (b) default Continue -> NO write, redirect via kit.hubExitTarget(request) first then await kit.nextTarget(request, page, scope) (next in section order = pp-027's commodity-bulk-details once it lands; until then nextTarget falls through per flow). Wrap the remove write in kit.recoverableSave(); marked persistence failure re-renders recoverableError: true status 500; other errors throw. The page collects NO user input — there is no Joi schema and no validation-error state; the only refusals are forged/stale indexes (no write, re-render 400). Exemplar file-for-file: sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.js.

Invalid/forged/stale index -> return null, controller performs no write.

increments.notes: 1:1 carry of inc-017 per MAPPING.json: a read-only echo of the commodityLines collection — NO new data captured, no new obligations, meta.collects = []. Primary recipe add-a-page for the registration spine, with the add-a-collection loop-page steps (§4.5/§4.7 of the cheat-sheet) governing the Remove branch; exemplar file-for-file is the live-animals consignment-details page (collects:[], per-row Remove submit inside the same POST, remove/post-remove.js action parsing — verified live this session, including its contract case at contract.test.js:213-222 which this increment's contract.plant-products.test.js case mirrors). DECISIONS (headless, recorded): (1) Remove operates at the SPECIES-row level — removeEntryAt(['commodityLines', i, 'species'], j) — matching the legacy remove_species_<id> semantics; the 'line's per-instance identity' in the planning brief is honoured as the row's (lineIndex, speciesIndex) pair validated at two levels per §8 G-B before any write. Whole-commodity-line removal is NOT offered on this page (legacy offers none; deselection of a code happens via commodity-search's reconcile, pp-023). (2) Cannot-remove-last parity kept: Remove suppressed when a line has one species ({{#gt variations.length 1}} in the legacy template). (3) One row per species; multiple varieties stack inside the Variety/Class cells (legacy complements were species-level rows; our depth-3 model can hold several varieties per species — stacking keeps 1 row = 1 removable entity, avoiding several Remove buttons with identical effect). (4) GOV.UK toolbox rulings from the page spec's nonStandardPatterns applied: govukTable macro (legacy hand-rolled table dropped govuk-table__row and carried the govuk-!margin-bottom-9 typo), no link-button class in either direction (Remove is an honest secondary submit button; 'Add another commodity' uses the Button component's href form), govuk-!-text-align-right over bespoke text-align-right, visually-hidden actions header renamed 'Actions' (legacy 'Remove action links' was a misnomer — they are buttons). (5) Blank Variety/Class cells, never the legacy 'None' literal (GDS content ruling flagged in the page spec; 'None' only reaches the cell when the fixture actually offers it as a variety option, in which case its label renders like any other). (6) No max-lines notice: SIBLING-SET-PLAN §3.3 declares policy.maxEntriesFrom = {} for CHED-PP, so the legacy cap state (env-configured, never traced) is deliberately not ported. (7) No check-answers work (pp-038), no mapper change (removal rides the existing whole-document PUT via pp-008's records service), no client JS, no webpack entry. (8) Continue label 'Save and continue' kept verbatim from the confirmed trace; the legacy three-way save routing (commodity_summary.js:47-53) is NOT ported — kit.nextTarget + section order own navigation here. Depth-3 reads/writes sit on P-7-proven ground (pp-012 gate) behind the pp-021 model-extension review.
openQuestions: Legacy renders this page ONLY when the chosen species carries variety/class reference data (the page-spec's central open question — 1 of 59 traced journeys reached it, and the spec recommends one deliberate trace: 08059000/CIDAC with no class chosen). This increment places the page unconditionally in the commodities section order per the plan's §2.1 page list; whether it should instead be conditionally skipped (or dropped in favour of the review page) is a design decision for the pp-021-adjacent review to confirm.

The legacy Remove control was never rendered in any trace and never exercised by any E2E test (template-inferred only); the cannot-remove-last suppression and immediate-removal-without-confirmation behaviours are therefore ported from template reading, not observed behaviour. The no-confirmation destructive remove matches the documents exemplar's house pattern, but flag for content/design review.

The 'Add another Genus (and Species)' link needs a line-context mechanism into commodity-basic-description; this plan defers to whatever line-targeting shape pp-024 shipped (query param vs path segment) — the implementor must match it exactly rather than invent a second convention.

filesToTouch.what: Add export const commodityBulkDetailsPage = { id: 'commodity-bulk-details', slug: 'commodity-bulk-details' }. File stays import-free (controller/flow both import the same object).

export const meta = { ...commodityBulkDetailsPage, collects: [] } (the commodityLines root is owned by commodity-search; members inherit dispatch coverage from the group — exemplar: live-animals consignment-details.controller.js:29). GET: state.get() once; state.collectionView(answers, ['commodityLines']) for facts; build per-line view rows (code + ref-data description from the pp-014 commodities service) prefilled from each entry's nine measure leaves; empty bulk panel. POST branches on the named submit action (documents-exemplar pattern — action travels as a submit button value so the crumb rides along, no GET mutation): (a) action='apply' — validate ≥1 line checkbox selected ('Select at least one commodity line to apply changes to') and ≥1 of the six bulk fields filled ('Fill in at least one field to update the selected commodity lines'); each FILLED bulk value also passes its field's format rule; then COPY each filled value onto every selected line via state.updateEntryAt(request, h, ['commodityLines'], index, entry) per selected index (copy-per-line, never apportion — v16 ruling) and 302 back to this page (server round-trip, zero client JS); bulk values are UI only, never persisted as answers. (b) action='clear' — re-render with an empty bulk panel, per-line values untouched (fixes the legacy Clear-by-reload trap; no write). (c) default Save and continue — validate EVERY line's measures with lib/validate factories (canonical strings in copyKeys); invalid → 400 re-render raw values; valid → commit each line in place via state.updateEntryAt wrapped in kit.recoverableSave (marked failure → recoverableError re-render 500; unexpected errors throw); exit via await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope) with kit.hubExitTarget(request) winning first. Every line index guarded before any write: Number.isInteger(index) && index >= 0 && index < lines.length — refuse forged/stale indexes with no write. finishedOrPropagated is rendered+validated only for lines whose commodity code the pp-014 fixture flags as requiring intended-use (plants-for-planting analogue); never commit a value for a line where the control did not render.

GET prefill from seeded lines; apply branch: values copied to selected lines only, unselected lines untouched, partial bulk fill copies only filled fields; 'Select at least one commodity line…' when none selected; 'Fill in at least one field…' when all six empty; clear branch resets bulk panel without touching line data; each per-line validation rule its own test (required x5, whole-number packages, quantity format, net-weight min/decimals/digits, finishedOrPropagated required-when-rendered); raw values + no commit on 400; cleaned commit via updateEntryAt + redirect on success; finishedOrPropagated absent (not rendered, not validated, not committed) for a non-flagged line; forged/out-of-range index refused with no write; recoverable-save failure → 500; unexpected error throws.

increments.notes: 1:1 carry of inc-019; closes m3. Follows the add-a-section recipe (cheat-sheet §3) in its one-page degenerate form: one page = one feature folder = one flow section = one task row = one hub spoke (spoke 4, §2.1). Exemplars: live-animals import-reason feature (smallest complete collecting page — controller/render/copy shape), transport section (section + task row + hub GROUPS wiring), origin e2e spec (per-rule validation + axe pattern), _species-quantities.njk (inputmode numeric idiom). Decisions applied, all grounded in the page spec + plan: (1) legacy page-optional/submit-required split on gross weight RESOLVED as model-mandatory (planningBrief says mandatory; c-018 single-layer validation means there is no second layer to defer to); required message uses GDS 'Enter the total gross weight' rather than legacy backend 'Add the total gross weight'. (2) gross>net rule gets ONE canonical wording — the legacy frontend string 'Total gross weight must be greater than the net weight' (page-spec discrepancies note asked Reconcile to pick one; the backend variant 'is less than' is discarded). (3) The legacy gross-weight-decimal phantom-field a11y defect is fixed by expressing the 5-decimal-places rule on the visible field with an anchorable message (page-spec openQuestion recommendation). (4) Unit persisted by CODE from pp-016's gross-volume-units.js, not the legacy hardcoded display string 'metres cubed' (page-spec openQuestion 5 decision). (5) Legacy presentation-table/table-responsive replaced by govukSummaryList without actions (page-spec govukAlternative; stays inside the govuk toolbox). (6) Rollups (net weight, packages) are DERIVED from commodityLines answers at render and never stored/sent (obligation-field-map inc-019 'derived — never stored'). (7) Legacy three-way exit collapsed: house kit.nextTarget/hub semantics; NO GMS interstitial (goods-movement is its own spoke, pp-031); review-change return is owned by the pp-038 check-answers Change machinery; back link is the house hubPath link, not href='#'. (8) CHED-P/D/A-only controls omitted per planningBrief. (9) Volume/unit pairing: presentGate gives unit-required-iff-volume in the MODEL; the reverse direction (unit posted without volume) is a controller fieldset rule per the house D-13 precedent — both directions validated in POST so no user input is silently dropped. (10) Check-answers rows for these fields are NOT built here — the check-answers feature is pp-038 (m4), which reads back every captured area; recipe step 5 is deliberately deferred to it. (11) obligation-field-map's inc-019 row also lists commodityComplement[].intendedForFinalUsers; that leaf is owned by pp-027 (commodity-bulk-details, matching its planningBrief) — recorded here so the duplicate mention is not double-built. (12) No etag equivalent: the records port is whole-document last-write-wins (Open Q 3 ruling in §6.2); lost-update protection is out of scope. Copy amounts to ~20 keys in both locales; e2e is one co-located spec plus a hub-spec extension.
openQuestions: Gross volume + unit are completely unexercised in legacy (no trace fills them, zero QA-repo references — page-spec openQuestion). Built here per the spec, but a BA could rule them dead surface and drop two controls; cheap question worth asking before or after build, non-blocking.

Exact stored codes for the two volume units are pp-016's call (e.g. LITRES / METRES_CUBED vs litres / m3); this increment consumes whatever gross-volume-units.js exports — confirm the module landed with codes, not display strings, before wiring the select.

Legacy 'does copy-as-new carry gross weight over / does mutating commodities clear it' is unresolved in the corpus (page-spec openQuestion). House model has no such implicit clearing — an out-of-scope-only wipe applies to grossVolumeUnit alone — but the copy-flow behaviour question transfers to pp-045 (copy-as-new), not here.

The 5-decimal-places bound and 16-char maxlength are inherited legacy limits; the maxlength cap is dropped (silent truncation is the defect the page spec flags) in favour of the numeric + decimal rules — flag if product wants an explicit upper-magnitude bound instead.

increments.notes: RATIONALE: completes the m0 hub skeleton (pp-007) to the ruled 12-spoke experience for everything built through m3. The build is a file-for-file transposition of the live-animals hub feature (G-C — no hub-from-scratch recipe): controller.js is the exemplar for GROUPS, STATUS_TAG, CANNOT_START, buildReviewItem, isHiddenRow and buildGroups; template.njk and copy bundles likewise. RULINGS APPLIED: FD-12 (review = flow section with authored gate scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers, NOT a task row — fixes the legacy hardcoded 'To do' review tag, the page spec's clearest defect); §2.1 (canonical row ids and spoke numbering — each spoke is its own numbered hub heading, so GROUPS degenerates deliberately to one row per group); standing deviations from chedpp-requirements.md: one stable id with status moves (journeyStrip caption replaces the legacy heading-tertiary DRAFT->CHEDPP flip), real-href back links (no href='#', no back-link+breadcrumbs duplication), govuk-frontend toolbox only (no phase-tag, no action-button/button-small). DECISIONS TAKEN HEADLESS: (1) GROUPS at this increment contains only the rows that exist (origin, purpose, commodities, additional-details, review) — rows for unbuilt sections land WITH their section increments per the planning brief; taskRowById on a missing row would throw, so the frame must not reference future rows. (2) Group-caption numbers are authored literally per §2.1 (live-animals precedent), so the rendered sequence reads 1,2,3,4,12 until m4/m5 fill the middle — a transient scaffolding state, accepted to keep the canonical numbers stable. (3) commodityTotals summary cards NOT transposed (live-animals-specific animal-count display; no CHED-PP requirement; read-only rollups belong to pp-028's additional-details page). (4) Attachments shortcut dropped (same target as the documents row, zero test coverage in legacy, spec flags it redundant). (5) Legacy prerequisite-gating of the hub (redirect-away when prerequisites incomplete) is NOT reproduced — reachability policy belongs to entry-guard.js (m0) and the 'complete in any order' promise; the target model's per-row Cannot-start/gate mechanics carry any genuine ordering constraints. (6) No 'Expired' status: the legacy Expired tag maps to no state in the target model (commodity-code validity is enforced at collection time via allowListed gates, not surfaced as a hub status). EXEMPLAR FILES: sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/{controller.js,template.njk,copy/copy.en.js,copy/copy.cy.js,hub.e2e.spec.js}; shared/kit.js (journeyStrip); flow/navigation.js (rowEntry/rowGatePasses/sectionEntry); flow/section-status.js; bridge/status/index.js. OVERLAP DISCIPLINE: earlier section increments (pp-018..pp-028) may already have added some GROUPS entries/row copy per recipe §3.6 — this increment brings the hub to the exact target state described here (idempotent reconciliation), and later increments (pp-030+) append theirs. Not platform-touching (diff confined to the set), so the two-sided live-animals check is not mandated; the full `npm test` step still exercises copy-parity/copy-convention across both sets.

export const meta = { ...transportBeforeBipPage, collects: ['borderControlPost', 'inspectionPremises', 'meansOfTransport', 'transportIdentification', 'transportDocumentReference', 'arrivalDate', 'arrivalTime', 'usesContainers', 'containers'] } (container members inherit the owning page from the group root). GET: state.get() ONCE; prefill from answers; premises select options resolved from bcps.js for the currently-answered/selected BCP (out-of-scope → not rendered); containers rows via state.collectionView(answers, ['containers']) — facts only, controller builds its own row view-models. POST branches on the submit action (documents-exemplar single-page loop): (a) action === 'add-container' → validate the entry row (at-least-one of containerNumber/sealNumber — controller fieldset rule, NOT model, house D-13 parity; max lengths 32/100) then state.appendEntry(request, h, 'containers', entry); (b) action === 'remove-container:<index>' → Number.isInteger index guard + look the instance up and refuse a forged/stale index, then state.removeEntry; (c) default Save/Continue → validate every in-scope field with factories from src/server/app/lib/validate/index.js — BCP membership rule built inside POST from the bcps.js fixture (never a frozen module-level schema), premises validated against the POSTed BCP's own allowlist (so a 400 re-render shows the premises options for the newly-chosen BCP — the no-JS way premises follows BCP), single-layer Joi with ONE canonical message per rule (c-018), arrivalDate real-date + window [today, today+90] inclusive, arrivalTime 24-hour validity; invalid → 400 re-render RAW values; valid → state.commit() cleaned values, kit.recoverableSave() (marked failure → recoverableError re-render 500, other errors throw), redirect via await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope). Never commit an out-of-scope value (engine wipes premises when the BCP changes off-allowlist, and container rows when usesContainers flips to No). All row/back/internal links wrapped in kit.withChangeContext. Copy via copyFor({ en, cy }); routes via kit.pageRoutes(page, { get, post }).

increments.notes: 1:1 carry of inc-027 as two add-a-page increments inside the traders feature group pp-035 created (recipe: sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md steps 1-12, with the plant ladder substituted per SIBLING-SET-PLAN §7; §2.1 spoke 10 fixes section id 'traders' and row id 'traders'). Exemplars: live-animals origin feature (multi-field collecting page with service-backed select + full validation set), live-animals features/confirmation (govuk-panel page markup), traders group's own traders-addresses page (pp-035) for the group file shape — its 'Add a consignor or exporter' link is the sole entry route to consignor-create (address-book search is bypassed until the pp-044 m5 stub, so NO 'Return to search' link is rendered on either page). Decisions taken headless: (a) the confirmation interstitial is KEPT per the canonical MAPPING brief even though consignor-create.json/consignor-confirmation.json both recommend dropping it — dropping is a cross-CHED design decision, not pp-local; in this model the consignor is already committed to the answers tree by consignor-create's save, so 'Add to notification' performs no write and simply returns to traders-addresses (no orphan-record problem, unlike IPAFFS's create-then-attach); (b) 'Select a country' replaces the legacy 'Enter a country' (GOV.UK select convention; the page spec itself recommends it) and also covers the forged-code case, replacing 'Country is not valid'; (c) consignorPostcode stays optional (frontend-Joi parity) and the label gains '(optional)' to fix the legacy unsignalled-optional defect; no country-conditional postcode rule (that would be NEW behaviour, not parity); (d) the 58-char city cap and 30-char telephone cap are carried deliberately (both unit-test-pinned in IPAFFS; likely TRACES constraints); (e) email/telephone mandatoriness is a frontend-only legacy rule (backend model has no @NotNull for them for ANY CHED type) — carried as the de-facto user contract; (f) no autocomplete token on the Country select, mirroring legacy (the values are non-pure-ISO codes like GB-ENG, so neither 'country' nor 'country-name' fits cleanly); (g) legacy artefacts NOT reproduced: title attributes on inputs, duplicated govuk-label class, heading-tertiary caption outside main, href='#' back link, the labelKey/article/displayType templating (all copy is literal strings in both locales); (h) country membership is controller-side validation against the pp-013 fixture built inside POST, not a model allowList gate — mirrors house handling of country selects; (i) obligation names are camelCase (path-safe answers keys per the manifest contract), not kebab. Not platform-touching (set files + the plant-owned contract clone only), so the two-sided live-animals check is not mandated; npm test still exercises the shared L1 suites.
openQuestions: City-or-town 58-character cap carried from legacy (every other text field is 255) — almost certainly a downstream TRACES/EU width constraint; confirm with the business before relaxing.

Confirmation interstitial kept per MAPPING, but both page specs recommend dropping it (attach-on-create + notification banner on traders-addresses); in this rebuild it is already write-free, so removing it later is copy/flow-only — flag to Sam/design as a cross-CHED simplification.

Postcode optionality: kept optional (legacy Joi parity) with an added '(optional)' label suffix; whether a mandatory postcode for GB addresses is the REAL requirement (legacy accepts a US ZIP against GB-ENG with no cross-field rule) is a business question — building that rule would be new behaviour.
Welsh strings for the new copy keys need content-design review (the legacy page had no Welsh at all; the copy here is first-cut translation).
Telephone format is deliberately unconstrained beyond max 30 (legacy parity); whether +44/spaced/international formats should be validated or normalised is a business question.
